skill.name: bullmq-specialist
skill.description: BullMQ guidance for Redis-backed job queues, background processing, scheduled work, worker patterns, and reliable async execution in Node.js and TypeScript applications.
skill.summary: Design and troubleshoot reliable BullMQ queues, workers, schedules, and job flows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline code formatting in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, credential access, network behavior, executable code, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed skill text.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 57 uses Markdown backticks around related skill names, not Ruby or shell command execution. The file is prompt-only and contains no executable script or command invocation.

content.value_statement: Teams can struggle with stuck jobs, retries, schedules, and Redis-backed worker behavior. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design and review BullMQ queue systems.
actual_capabilities: Designs production-ready BullMQ queue and worker setups.
Explains delayed jobs, scheduled jobs, priorities, and rate limits.
Plans job flows with dependencies and parent-child relationships.
Reviews worker concurrency, events, retries, and dead letter handling.
Identifies queue anti-patterns such as giant payloads and infinite concurrency.
limitations: Does not run Redis, BullMQ, or application code by itself.
Needs project context to tune concurrency, retry, and rate limit settings.
Focuses on BullMQ and Redis, not every message broker or workflow engine.
Cannot inspect live queue metrics unless the user provides them.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Queue System
use_cases.description: Create a BullMQ design for asynchronous work, retries, delayed jobs, and worker boundaries before implementation.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Production Job Failures
use_cases.description: Review stuck jobs, retry behavior, Redis pressure, and worker settings to find likely causes and fixes.

use_cases.title: Modernize Background Processing
use_cases.description: Convert ad hoc cron tasks or inline work into structured BullMQ queues, schedules, and flows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Queue
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new background job queue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a basic BullMQ queue for this Node.js task. Include the queue purpose, worker behavior, retry policy, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Worker Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing worker configuration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my BullMQ worker design for concurrency, rate limits, retries, and Redis impact. Point out risks and suggest practical improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Scheduled Jobs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for delayed or repeatable work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a BullMQ approach for delayed and repeatable jobs in my application. Include scheduling strategy, idempotency rules, and observability needs.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Job Flows
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design for dependent multi-step processing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a BullMQ FlowProducer architecture for this multi-step workflow. Include dependencies, failure behavior, compensation steps, and monitoring points.

output_examples.input: I need to process uploaded videos after users submit them.
output_examples.output: Recommends separate queues for upload validation, transcoding, thumbnail creation, and notification. Defines retry rules, idempotency keys, and monitoring signals.

output_examples.input: Our jobs are stuck and Redis CPU is high.
output_examples.output: Lists likely causes such as excessive concurrency, large payloads, slow processors, and missing backoff. Suggests checking queue metrics and worker logs first.

output_examples.input: We need daily digest emails with retries and rate limits.
output_examples.output: Proposes repeatable scheduling, bounded concurrency, per-provider rate limits, dead letter handling, and clear event logging for failed deliveries.

best_practices: Keep job payloads small and store large data in durable application storage.
Make processors idempotent so retries do not duplicate external side effects.
Set explicit concurrency, retry, backoff, and dead letter behavior for each queue.
anti_patterns: Do not use giant job payloads for files, records, or nested business data.
Do not rely on infinite concurrency to fix throughput problems.
Do not skip dead letter handling for important background work.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design, review, and troubleshoot BullMQ queues, workers, schedules, retries, events, and job flows.

faq.question: Can it generate BullMQ implementation code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation patterns and suggest code structure when the user asks for code-oriented help.

faq.question: Does it require Redis expertise?
faq.answer: Basic Redis context helps, but the skill explains Redis-related queue concerns in practical terms.

faq.question: Can it debug live production queues?
faq.answer: It can reason from logs, metrics, configuration, and symptoms provided by the user. It cannot inspect systems directly.

faq.question: Is it useful for scheduled jobs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers delayed jobs, repeatable jobs, scheduling behavior, and operational safeguards.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Backend engineers, platform teams, and technical leads who manage Redis-backed background processing can use it.
